seo_title: Cost of Living in Limassol 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Limassol per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Cyprus's main IT hub, with a large Russian-speaking diaspora and a thriving fintech scene. A Mediterranean climate and English in everyday life, but high prices and tricky banking.
pros: Europe's leading fintech and crypto hub for Russian speakers
English is effectively the second everyday language
A large Russian-speaking community in IT
cons: Very expensive rent — higher than central Moscow
Difficulties opening a bank account for Russians
High taxes and a mandatory corporate structure
A small island — you can only fly out via Athens or Dubai

visa_steps.title: Tourist visa
visa_steps.description: A 90-day Pro Visa for Russians — issued online before arrival.

visa_steps.title: Open Permit (category F)
visa_steps.description: A residence permit for the financially independent — requires a €30,000 deposit and income of €24,000+ per year.

visa_steps.title: Employment Permit
visa_steps.description: Through a job at a Cypriot company or through your own firm.

visa_steps.title: Setting up a company
visa_steps.description: A Cypriot LTD is set up by a lawyer in 2–4 weeks, with €1 minimum capital.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic Bank — hard for Russians without a local firm and a lawyer.

faq.question: Can I just arrive and rent an apartment in Limassol?
faq.answer: Only for 90 days on a Pro Visa. Longer stays require a residence permit, ideally through a company.

faq.question: What's the situation with banks in Limassol?
faq.answer: Very difficult for Russians. Realistically only via a lawyer + a Cypriot LTD + due diligence.

faq.question: What are the taxes in Limassol?
faq.answer: Income tax 0–35%, with a non-dom exemption for new residents — no tax on dividends and passive income.

faq.question: Do I need English in Limassol?
faq.answer: English is enough for everyday life. Greek helps with paperwork but isn't required.

faq.question: Where should I live in Limassol?
faq.answer: The seafront is premium. Germasogeia and Kolossi are calmer and cheaper. Dherynia is good for families.

faq.question: How is healthcare in Limassol?
faq.answer: GeSY is the state insurance for residents. Private cover starts from €1,500/year.

reviews.text: Limassol is ideal for remote work in IT/fintech. The downside — banks demand the maximum paperwork, all through a lawyer.
Sea, English, calm. But rent doubled in two years — the market is overheated by relocators.
